findings.summary: Pinned Dawn and Doe each pass the unchanged 16-assertion World Labs workload, record all 13 shader attempts and eight getCompilationInfo results, and retain exactly one error-bearing compilation result. The error in both lanes is bound to the identical LF-normalized runtime shader source hash sha256:53672fc645bfd78a8635f16261c9212ad39fc1b12aa95caaf3557221f16632ce.

The two lanes share diagnostic-source identity ac1fac8956bb06127283231c1fb26d9f2d9b64277eb519c6fef1342adce60197 as well as normalized command-shape and mapped-output identity. Dawn reports the missing struct member at line 6, column 15; Doe reports its Vulkan WGSL-to-SPIR-V compilation failure. Wording and location fidelity are retained as evidence but are not conflated with semantic source identity.

limitations: The result proves a public JavaScript WebGPU diagnostic binding, not native-driver tracing, filesystem or network closure, or operating-system dependency identity.
Provider-specific diagnostic wording and source-position precision differ and are not claimed equivalent.
The lanes use workspace source modules and one clean process per provider rather than clean-installed release packages or promotion stress populations.
The result cannot reopen the terminal World Labs runtime-ownership decision and grants no performance, promotion, release, or runtime-ownership credit.

runtimeOwnershipAssessment.summary: The compilation-observer successor is diagnostic infrastructure evidence only. The earlier governed-incumbent result remains the terminal ownership adjudication.

teardown.summary: Both governed application processes exit without crash, hang, or timeout.

stress.summary: One clean process per provider is below promotion stress floors.

memory.summary: Peak process-tree RSS is observed, but bounded same-process growth is not measured.

receipts.summary: The result binds the plan, observer, schema, providers, application assertions, exact shader source, compilation results, commands, and mapped outputs.

replay.summary: Pinned Dawn and Doe reproduce the same frozen application behavior and diagnostic source identity.

ownership.summary: The successor is forbidden from reopening the completed ownership decision.

release.summary: World Labs remains a non-blocking diagnostic application.
